task: Turn a CAD model written in Python into a 3D-printable STL
packaging_note: No upstream container; the project's cadgen release wheel on Python 3.13 with the system libraries Open CASCADE needs, telemetry off

inputs.what: a build123d model script: one or more @cadgen.model functions, and a __main__ block that calls cadgen.export(part, Path('/work/outputs/<name>.stl')) for each part

outputs.what: one STL per exported part, named by the script

known_issues: `cadgen export <name>` fails with 'is no document': document ids exist only while the engine runs, so export from the script under `cadgen run` instead
Upstream telemetry is on by default; the image turns it off and runs have no network
The image is about 3 GB, mostly Open CASCADE

x-display.title: Export a CAD script for 3D printing
x-display.summary: Run a build123d Python model and export its parts as STL files.
x-display.description: Use this when you already have a model script and need geometry you can open in a slicer. Your script defines the parts and exports them; UGT supplies the environment that runs it. A written description alone is not a model script.
